o: Values lie in [-50, 50], so keep a frequency bucket of size 101 for the current window. To get the x-th smallest, walk buckets from -50 upward accumulating counts until reaching x; if fewer than x negatives exist overall, output 0. Slide the window by adding the incoming element and removing the outgoing one. Example [-3,1,2,-3,0,-3], k=2, x=1: window [1,2] has zero negatives → 0; others yield -3.
k: Value range is tiny (101 buckets), so selection by bucket scan is O(51) regardless of k.
Only negative values matter; if the window holds fewer than x negatives the beauty is 0.

a.i: Maintain counts per value and the number of negatives; the x-th smallest negative is found by scanning buckets from -50 up.
s: Fill the first window's counts; track negCount.
For each window start, if negCount < x append 0, else scan values -50..-1 accumulating counts until >= x and record that value.
Slide: decrement outgoing, increment incoming, adjusting negCount.
a.t: O(n · 50) — bucket scan per window, independent of k

w: The tiny value range is the entire trick; heaps or ordered sets would be slower and messier. Pitfall: the scan must cover only negative values (stop at -1) and the early-exit condition uses cumulative counts. Follow-up: general values would need an indexed multiset or merge-sort tree.
